answers.answer: Redis is a server program that keeps data primarily in memory (main goal: an in-memory database) and lets applications read and change it over a network; clients send commands such as SET/GET that run against in-memory data structures (strings, hashes, lists, sets, sorted sets, streams, vector sets, module types). Writes can optionally be copied to disk (snapshots/AOF) and to replicas. Stated uses: caching, session management, querying/sorting/analytics, messaging and interservice communication, vector operations (plus per-type uses: counters, leaderboards, rate limiters, queues, event sourcing, similarity search/RAG).
answers.where: Overview intro; Core ideas; data-types table; Advantages the maintainers state

answers.answer: Snapshots (RDB) dump the data set to disk via a forked child (rdbSaveBackground/rdbSave, triggered by save points in serverCron or BGSAVE); the AOF logs every write command (feedAppendOnlyFile into aof_buf, flushed in beforeSleep), with appendfsync always making the write reach the file before the reply. Both can be on, or off. Durability comparison beyond that: not stated (the trade-off details are withheld). At startup loadDataFromDisk loads the AOF (loadAppendOnlyFiles) when AOF is on, otherwise the RDB; a preload-file setting overrides both.

answers.answer: src/bio.c worker threads do background close(2), AOF fsync and lazy freeing (freeObjAsync frees in the background only above LAZYFREE_THRESHOLD=64). Ordering guarantee: not stated.

answers.answer: Modules are shared libraries that extend Redis and add new commands (modules API). They are named with loadmodule (config line reaches queueLoadModule at startup) and main calls moduleLoadFromQueue (outside Sentinel mode); bundled modules are pinned in modules/modules.yaml, fetched with make modules-update and configured via redis-full.conf. Loading into an already running server (e.g. at runtime command) and how a module data type is saved/restored: not stated (src/module.c is withheld).

answers.answer: The event loop (aeMain in src/ae.c) repeatedly calls aeProcessEvents, which runs beforeSleep, waits in aeApiPoll (best of evport/epoll/kqueue/select), runs afterSleep, then runs ready file events (read handler before write handler unless AE_BARRIER) and time events (serverCron, server.hz times/sec: active expiry, rehashing, saves, replication reconnect). Connection layer: connSocketAcceptHandler accepts and calls acceptCommonHandler, which creates a client via createClient and installs readQueryFromClient as the read handler; readQueryFromClient reads into querybuf, processInputBuffer parses and calls processCommand; replies are buffered and sent from beforeSleep via handleClientsWithPendingWrites (after flushAppendOnlyFile). A generic connection-type abstraction layer: not stated.

answers.answer: Type is what a value is (an abstract data structure such as a list, defined also by operations' space/time complexity); encoding is how it is represented in memory at the moment (e.g. strings RAW/EMBSTR/INT, sets INTSET/HT, lists QUICKLIST of listpacks, streams radix tree of listpacks). Both exist so memory-saving encodings can sit under each type. Who decides which encoding is used: not stated (withheld, rests on redis.conf).

answers.answer: Code split: src/cluster.c (key-to-slot mapping, routing/redirection, getNodeByQuery) and src/cluster_legacy.c (node failure detection, failover, bus). keyHashSlot computes crc16 of the key (only the {...} hashtag part if present), low 14 bits -> one of 16384 slots. processCommand calls getNodeByQuery, which returns the node serving that slot; if it is this node the command runs, otherwise clusterRedirectClient replies MOVED (or ASK during migration) with slot and node address; cross-slot keys get -CROSSSLOT, -TRYAGAIN during migration.
answers.where: Workflow 5; Mechanisms table 'Cluster'; Glossary hash-slot; Trade-offs distribution

answers.answer: Accept (connSocketAcceptHandler -> acceptCommonHandler, rejects at maxclients; createClient installs readQueryFromClient; clientAcceptHandler refuses non-loopback clients in protected mode with no default-user password) -> Read (aeProcessEvents calls readQueryFromClient, bytes into querybuf) -> Parse (processInputBuffer: '*' = multibulk, else inline) -> Dispatch (main thread calls processCommandAndResetClient -> processCommand; I/O threads only queue the client) -> Gate (lookupCommand and checks) -> Execute (call -> c->cmd->proc, e.g. setCommand -> setGenericCommand, setKeyByLink, server.dirty++) -> Propagate (dirty changed so alsoPropagate; propagateNow feeds feedAppendOnlyFile and replicationFeedSlaves; multiple commands wrapped in MULTI/EXEC) -> Flush (beforeSleep runs flushAppendOnlyFile first; with appendfsync always the write reaches the file before the reply) -> Reply (handleClientsWithPendingWrites/writeToClient). Checks that can stop it: authentication (noautherr), ACL (-NOPERM), cluster routing (redirect), memory/maxmemory eviction failure for deny-on-memory-limit commands (OOM), disk errors (writeCommandsDeniedByDiskError), read-only replica (roslaveerr), loading (loadingerr); also MULTI queuing.
answers.where: Workflow 2; 'Main checks in processCommand' table; Deep dive propagation

answers.answer: When the AOF grows past auto-aof-rewrite-percentage and auto-aof-rewrite-min-size, serverCron calls rewriteAppendOnlyFileBackground, which forks a child. The step-by-step rewrite details beyond that: not stated. File tracking: a manifest file names which files are current: one BASE (snapshot from last rewrite), one or more ordered INCR files (writes since last successful rewrite); after a rewrite old BASE and INCR become HISTORY, removed automatically unless garbage collection is disabled.
answers.where: Workflow 3 'Compact the log'; Deep dive AOF lifecycle; Figure 'Life of the AOF files'

answers.answer: replicationCron calls connectWithMaster (syncWithMaster handler); the replica sends PSYNC with replication ID and offset (slaveTryPartialResynchronization). On the master, syncCommand calls masterTryPartialResynchronization: if the ID matches and the offset is still in the backlog, it answers +CONTINUE and sends only the missing data (partial resync); otherwise +FULLRESYNC, the master runs startBgsaveForReplication and the replica receives the RDB in readSyncBulkPayload. Afterwards replicationFeedSlaves streams write commands; a replica relays its master's stream unchanged to its own replicas.
answers.where: Workflow 4; figure 'How a replica catches up'

answers.answer: Two mechanisms: lazy, on access expireIfNeeded deletes an expired key (src/db.c), and active, activeExpireCycle scans in the background (src/expire.c, run from serverCron). How the active cycle limits its own cost: not stated. Consistency: a replica does not expire keys itself; it waits for the master, which sends synthesized DEL operations through the shared replication/AOF feed.

answers.answer: Redis uses a mostly single-threaded core; scaling across cores is done by higher-order features like Redis Cluster (rationale for single-thread beyond that: not stated). Extra threads: I/O threads read and parse (new client assigned to the least-loaded I/O thread) but cannot run commands; pub/sub, monitor, blocked and tracking clients stay on the main thread; bio threads do background close, AOF fsync and lazy freeing; forked children write RDB/AOF rewrites. Costs/conditions: io-threads does not make commands run in parallel (throughput limit); TLS.md says multi-threaded I/O is not supported for TLS (possibly outdated); helper threads start after modules load due to an ld.so TLS/dlopen race; forked children add copy-on-write memory pressure.
answers.where: Core ideas; Deep dive threads; Trade-offs

answers.answer: Sync policy trade-off: only partly stated: with appendfsync always the write reaches the file before the reply, and a failed write ends the process (exit(1)) because the reply may already be buffered and cannot be rolled back; other policies' trade-offs are withheld. The log is flushed in beforeSleep so that the write reaches the file before replies are sent in the same pass (flush runs first, then handleClientsWithPendingWrites). Durability given up during a background save with the mitigation on: not stated.

answers.answer: When maxmemory is set, processCommand calls performEvictions before running a command; if it cannot free memory, commands marked deny-on-memory-limit are refused with an OOM error, while read-only/non-memory commands still run; the eviction policy may forbid eviction (noeviction). A 32-bit instance with no limit gets 3 GB maxmemory with noeviction. Forked children add copy-on-write memory not covered by figures. Which memory/instances are exempt from the limit: otherwise not stated.
